  { key: 'R-W0', dir: 'C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-r-w0', units: ['W0-1/W0-2'], scope: 'app/utils/url_validator.py + app/services/database_service.py: (W0-1b) memoise a gaierror only for EAI_NONAME (and EAI_NODATA where defined); EAI_AGAIN and other codes fail closed for this call only; record time.monotonic() inside _resolve at start and memoise a timeout only when the resolve genuinely ran past the deadline (not when it was queued); a slow-but-successful resolve is a positive memo, never a negative one - pins for all three shapes, both flag states, flag OFF byte-identical; (W0-2b) the shared transport under ENABLE_SUPABASE_CLIENT_REUSE uses http2=False (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive pool, one request per connection) so a hung PostgREST call cannot head-of-line-block unrelated requests and the read timeout bounds each call - pin with a local fake server that hangs one request while another completes; also pin the OFF-path construction (anon and user clients) that the reviewer found unpinned (M13/M14). const UNITS = GROUPS.filter((g) => !ONLY || ONLY.includes(g.key))

const RED_SCHEMA = { type: 'object', required: ['unit', 'test_files_written', 'failing_count', 'failures_are_right_reason', 'failure_evidence', 'comm_base', 'measurements_run', 'spec_disagreements'], properties: {
  unit: { type: 'string' }, test_files_written: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, failing_count: { type: 'integer' }, failures_are_right_reason: { type: 'boolean' },

  measurements_run: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, spec_disagreements: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } } }

  mutation_checks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, comm_gate: { type: 'string' }, flag_identity: { type: 'string', description: 'for each flag: OFF byte-identical proof; for unflagged: the additive/identity proof' },
  measurements_run: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, pr_text: { type: 'string' }, deviations_from_spec: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, git_status_final: { type: 'string' }, residual_risk: { type: 'string' } } }

- W1-8c: the three consume `except asyncio.TimeoutError` branches (sitemap, jsonapi, the _new_adapter_specs loop) are silent, so a budget-clamped consume under the genuine-priority flag drops a whole family with no line. _timeout_none cannot see an inner timeout the adapter swallowed (M13-34 clamps inner fetches to 9 s under the 10 s wrap). It also logs a TimeoutError the adapter raised 10 ms in as `TIMEOUT after 10.0s`.
- W1-8d: the ERROR drop line writes str(exc) verbatim. Probe P4 gave a 200,136-character record containing a proxy password and a raw newline.

FIX (app/services/structured_comparison_service.py only; no return value changes):
- Per-scraper failure, one INFO line: `[ADAPTER DROP] fanout:<curl|firecrawl|scrapedo>:<retailer_domain>: ERROR <Type>: <_safe_exc text>`. It carries the retailer label as the scraper receives it, never the scraped URL. The DEBUG `{url} raised` lines are gone.
- Per-wave summary after fan_out returns: `[FANOUT] wave=<curl|render> completed=N failed=N cancelled=N elapsed=S`, where completed = wave size - failed - cancelled.
- On the wave's budget TimeoutError: `[FANOUT] wave=<kind> TIMEOUT pending=N elapsed=S`, where pending = wave size (fan_out's own counts are lost when it is cancelled).
- Consume branches: `[ADAPTER DROP] <sitemap|jsonapi|woo|salla|occ|...>: CONSUME-BOUND after <bound>s`. The bound is the one actually waited under, captured with a walrus at the existing `_consume_bound()` call.
- _timeout_none is timed with time.monotonic():
  - wrap timeout, logged only when elapsed >= timeout - 0.05: `TIMEOUT after <elapsed>s`
  - earlier TimeoutError: `ERROR TimeoutError (adapter-raised)`
  - None at or after adapter_inner_ceiling() - 0.5: `SLOW-MISS after <elapsed>s`
  - fast misses and every hit stay silent; cancellation is still never caught and never logged.
- New local `_safe_exc(exc)`: it removes URL userinfo up to the last '@' before the host, drops the query string and fragment, and keeps host and path. Every line break (including U+2028/U+2029 and \x0b) becomes one space, and the text is cut to 200 chars. It scrubs before truncating. It is applied to the _timeout_none ERROR line and to the new fanout lines.
  - Why not the W1-1 helper: it was measured to be unfit. sentry_service._scrub_query_string keeps api_key= and never strips userinfo.

FAILED_COUNT IS NOT THE PRODUCTION SIGNAL. failed_count keeps its semantics. Production scrapers still catch their fetch errors and return None, so the summary's failed= stays 0 for real fetch failures; only an exception that escapes a scraper (a bug) raises it. The production failure signal is the per-scraper `[ADAPTER DROP] fanout:` lines. The W5 STEP-0 canary must count `[ADAPTER DROP] fanout:` lines (and `CONSUME-BOUND` / `SLOW-MISS` / `TIMEOUT` lines), not failed=.
